creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Display Resolution

description: Calculate the framebuffer size of five displays and a custom one, and judge whether each fits in the Pico's 264 KB of RAM.

learningObjectives: Calculate framebuffer memory from width, height and bits per pixel
Evaluate whether a display's framebuffer fits in the Pico's 264 KB of RAM
Compare the memory cost of monochrome and color displays

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculation and judgment against a limit
keyQuestions: Why does a color pixel need 16 times the memory of a monochrome pixel?
Why is 200 KB a safer limit than 264 KB?
What happens to memory when width and height both double?
commonMisconceptions: Memory grows with the screen width only (it grows with width times height)
All 264 KB are free for the framebuffer (MicroPython and your code need RAM too)
assessmentOpportunities: The student computes 128 x 64 x 1 / 8 = 1,024 bytes.
The student explains why 360 x 360 at 16 bpp leaves almost no RAM for the program.
The student proposes a way to fit a large display (lower bpp or partial buffers).
